terms.meaning: A team a user picks from real players, scored by how those players perform.
Two players with bonus scoring, one of them the leader of the team.
A budget value each player costs, with a total cap for the team.
A player who both bats and bowls well.

The eleven players in a cricket team on the field.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Shared rule numbers
sections.what: Sets the team size at eleven and the credit cap at 100.
sections.why: The team builder and the server both read these numbers, so they agree.
sections.watch_out: Changing these numbers changes both sides, so they must be released together.

sections.name: ROLE_LIMITS
sections.title: Minimum and maximum players per role
sections.what: Sets how many batters, bowlers, all-rounders and wicketkeepers a team may have.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps teams balanced like a real cricket side.
sections.watch_out: A role missing from this list is not counted, so the role check can be bypassed.

sections.name: ROLE_NAMES, RulePlayer, TeamCheck
sections.title: Role display names and types
sections.what: Gives friendly plural names for each role for error messages, and defines the shapes of a player and of a validation result.
sections.watch_out: A new role must be added to both the names list and the limits list.

sections.name: validateFantasyTeam
sections.title: Checking a whole team
sections.what: Checks a submitted team in order: correct size, no duplicates, all players found, captain and vice-captain in the team and different, players from the two match teams, credits under the cap, and role counts within limits. Returns ok or the first error.
sections.why: Likely reason: checking in a fixed order means the first error is the simplest one to fix.
sections.watch_out: Players with an unlisted role are not checked for role, so a team with such players can pass.

summary: The shared rules for building a fantasy cricket team: size, credit cap, role counts, captain and vice-captain.
purpose: It decides whether a submitted team is allowed, so bad teams are refused before they are saved.
why: Likely reason: the team builder on the page and the server must apply exactly the same rules.
how: It holds the team size, credit cap and role limits. The validation step checks the team in a set order: size, duplicates, players found, captain and vice-captain, match sides, credit cap, and role counts. It returns the first problem it finds, or ok.
inputs: The chosen player ids, captain and vice-captain, the player details with role and credits, and the two team names of the match.
outputs: Either ok, or an error message naming the first problem.
risks: A player whose role is not in the limits list is not counted against any role, so a team with unknown roles can pass.
debug: Read the error message: it names the first rule broken. If a valid team is refused, check the player data passed in, including its role spelling and credits.
